title: Planned Europe and South America trips; work after Celestin's death
summary: Plans to take the band to Europe and South America collapsed when Celestin died; work dropped and then recovered under Eddie Pearson.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Was that in the Absinthe House?

At the Absinthe House. That's where it was. Yeah. So I had been with the band for quite a while before Papa died. And I'm sorry he passed so early because they were making preparation to take us to Europe. Yeah. We were making voyage to Europe. But after Papa died, well it looked like it kind of, all that kind of passed away. Yeah. Yeah. Otherwise we'd been going to Europe now. Then one group was thinking about sending us to South America. stuff like stuff

They were going to get a group of South American dancers and the band was going to rehearsal and they were going to make a larger band, you see, and go to South America. But that went through too after Popper died.
Do you still play the same number of jobs you had when Popper was alive, or do you find that the work is getting less and less?

No, they got less. They got less. Yeah, they got less, yes. Now, after Popper died and Eddie taking over, we've done almost as much as with Popper had. Yeah? With Eddie? Yeah, with Eddie Pearson. And after he died, well, it looked like it sliced up a little bit more then, you see. And so...
